summary: Replaced `beforeRegisterNodeDef` + `onNodeCreated` prototype chaining with `comfy.defs.extend('FastPreview', …)`. The two `api.addEventListener` preview subscriptions, the module-level `execId` written from the `executing` event, the `serverSupportsFeature('supports_preview_metadata')` probe and the `displayNodeId === this.id` test all collapse into `b.onPreview`, which delivers frames already correlated to the node — so `addEventListener`/`removeEventListener` are obsolete, not dropped. `node.imgs = [img]` + `setDirtyCanvas` become a `widgets.canvas` draw plus `redraw()`, which renders under both renderers. Per-node state is a Map keyed by `node.id`, cleared in `b.onRemoved`.

test:
equivalence — a FastPreview node still ends up 550x550 on creation, and a
preview frame addressed to that node still results in exactly one image being
displayed on the node (one image object retained per node, replaced on each
new frame). Loading the extension registers behaviour for the type
'FastPreview' and for no other type. Removing the node releases the per-node
preview state so no listener or image is retained. All of this holds on the
original source and on the converted source.

fix — with TWO FastPreview nodes previewing during the same run on a server
that does NOT report supports_preview_metadata, emit a plain `b_preview`
event while `executing` last named node A. On the ORIGINAL source both nodes'
plainHandler compare the single module-level `execId` against their own id,
so the frame is attributed by a global that is shared between them: node B
shows nothing while node A shows the frame, and if `executing` has already
advanced to B when A's frame arrives late, A's frame is shown on B —
mis-attribution. Asserting "each node only ever displays frames the backend
produced for it" FAILS on the original. On the CONVERTED source there is no
module-level `execId`: `onPreview` delivers each frame already correlated to
its own node handle, so the assertion PASSES.

Second fix claim: the original writes `node.imgs = [img]` and calls
`setDirtyCanvas`, which renders only under the legacy canvas renderer. Under
Nodes 2.0 the original displays nothing; the converted source draws through
`widgets.canvas`, which renders under both. Asserting "the preview is visible
with the legacy renderer disabled" fails before and passes after.

wire format — neither source adds, removes or reorders widgets that
serialize: the mounted canvas widget carries no value, and no widget value or
link is touched, so `graphToPrompt` output and the serialized workflow are
byte-identical between the two sources.
